items.topic: Primary fix layer: where does the normalization live?
items.context: Spec proposes three options. Per the spec, you preferred B (API-side) to avoid papering over ergonomics at the CLI layer. Confirming so the plan can commit. Note: choosing B does not preclude minor CLI display polish.

options.label: CLI sugar only — accept --selected=proposed and translate to legacy payload
options.rationale: Smallest change, but leaves the API contract semantically wrong; future clients still see the awkward shape

options.label: API normalizes — single-proposal decisions don't require --selected at all
options.rationale: Fixes the contract at the source; CLI and UI both benefit; matches the operator's stated preference and the three-surface parity rule

options.label: decision-add auto-populates a default option for single-proposal decisions
options.rationale: Avoids changing accept logic, but pollutes data model with synthetic options; misleading on read

items.context: Once the API accepts a single-proposal decision without --selected, the accepted decision needs a stored marker so decision-show, audit logs, and queries can render the outcome. Two clean options.

options.label: Boolean field on the decision: accepted_as_proposed: true
options.rationale: Explicit, queryable, and orthogonal to the existing selected/freeform fields; reads cleanly in JSON dumps

options.label: Reuse selected with sentinel string "proposed"
options.rationale: Smaller schema change; existing display code mostly works; risk: "proposed" leaks into option-key namespace and may be surprising

options.label: Both — boolean for clarity, plus selected="proposed" for legacy display compatibility
options.rationale: Belt-and-suspenders; redundant but bridges old code that assumes selected is set

items.topic: Treatment of the legacy --selected=__other__ --freeform="accept as proposed" pattern
items.context: Greenfield default would reject the old pattern with a clear error. But existing stored decisions already carry that shape — they need to be readable. The decision is about WRITES (new accepts), not reads.

options.label: Reject loudly on write — return 400 with helpful migration message
options.rationale: Greenfield-pure; forces operator to learn the new pattern; reads of historical data are still tolerant via decision-show normalization

options.label: Silently accept as alias — translate __other__ + accept-as-proposed freeform to the new shape
options.rationale: Most permissive; zero friction; but hides the API contract change and weakens the greenfield commitment

options.label: Warn + accept — log a deprecation warning but still process the request
options.rationale: Middle ground; useful if other automated callers exist that you can't easily update

items.topic: Should decision-add gain an explicit --single-proposal flag?
items.context: Today, single-proposal decisions are inferred from an empty options[] array. We could keep that implicit signal or add an explicit flag (--single-proposal or --no-options) so intent is captured at creation time. This is orthogonal to D1 but lives in the same surface.

options.label: Stay implicit — empty options[] means single-proposal, no new flag
options.rationale: Smaller change; the data model already encodes intent; one less flag to remember

options.label: Add --single-proposal flag that asserts options must be empty
options.rationale: Makes intent explicit; catches mistakes (operator who meant to add options but forgot); slightly more typing

options.label: Add an enum kind field on Decision (single_proposal | multi_option) — empty options is invalid for multi_option
options.rationale: Strongest typing; biggest change; probably overkill for the current scale

items.text: Initiative context: this fix is one of 4 pending members of prompt-manager-decision-workflow-polish (2 already completed: deferral primitive, partial-accept-with-modifications). Sibling fix `decision-show-options-default-output` will overlap with this plan on display formatting — the executing agent should coordinate so single-proposal decisions render consistently across both PRs.

The initiative description specifies a three-surface parity rule: all decision-workflow work must ship across API + CLI + UI together. The plan reflects this — Phase 1/2/3 cover all three surfaces in one PR. Do not partial-ship.

plan_updates: Created initial plan.md scaffold with all 13 mandatory sections plus a Greenfield Constraint section, a Cross-Initiative Implications section, and a Cleanup & Verification phase. Approach committed to option B per spec preference; storage marker, legacy-write treatment, and decision-add explicitness deferred to D2/D3/D4 in this round.
